name: Code Mycelial Network Specification
synopsis: Code Mycelial Network (CMN) specification — normative documents, JSON schemas, and conformance test vectors for sovereign code distribution
intent: Provide the complete normative specification for the Code Mycelial Network protocol — seven chapters covering Substrate (discovery & identity), Mycelium (domain manifest), Spore (package format), Taste (safety evaluation), Strain (conventions), URI (addressing), and Algorithm Registry

Ship machine-readable JSON Schema definitions (cmn.json, mycelium.json, spore-core.json, spore.json, taste.json) for validating all protocol artifacts, plus conformance test vectors (merkle, signature, uri, capsule, taste gating, key rotation, bond traversal) so implementers can verify correctness without reading prose
mutations: Add a design-rationale section to 01-substrate §1.1 explaining why CMN anchors identity to a domain rather than a bare public key: domain registration imposes a continuous real-world cost that is the network's primary sybil-resistance mechanism (the reason Nostr retrofitted NIP-05 onto bare-pubkey identities), presented as a deliberate trade-off rather than inherited centralization

Document the continuity-versus-verifiability trade-off of domain-bound identity — a lapsed, seized, or transferred domain forfeits first-class trust bootstrapping for new clients and discovery, but does not weaken the verifiability of already-published content, which stays content-addressed and embeds core.key so any holder of the bytes can verify signatures and hashes without the origin domain being reachable

Decouple protocol version from the schema hostname — the version is the /v1/ segment of a payload's $schema URL path plus the document-type filename, and the hostname (cmn.dev or any mirror) MUST NOT influence trust, version selection, or validation; cmn.dev is the reference publisher of the schema bundle, not the owner of the namespace, so mirrored schema URLs with the same version segment and filename denote the same version

Restructure 01-substrate §6 into Version Identity / Version Determination / Migration Rules — add a canonical $schema table per document type, require rejecting any payload whose $schema does not resolve by version segment and document-type filename to a recognized version, and clarify that the resolvable $schema URL is a tooling affordance while normative validation MUST use embedded schemas rather than a network fetch

Consolidate the standalone overview.md into the spec README (RFC 2119/8174 normative language, role-based reading paths, document map, versioning pointers), remove overview.md as a redundant document and update the conformance README's non-normative list, and annotate Schema references across the substrate, mycelium, and spore chapters as hostname-non-authoritative
